summary: Dominik Wujastyk specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at the University of London and University of Oxford, he held posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1982–2004), UCL (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2015), and the University of Alberta (2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1978–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1988.
Dominique-Sila Khan worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and was a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University (attested 2001).

Don Handelman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2008).
Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Wilhelm Geiger.

Donald A. Ringe specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bard College, the University of Oxford, Yale University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he joined the linguistics faculty around 1985.

Donald Capps worked in religious studies, studying at Lewis & Clark College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held positions at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte (~1974–1981) and Princeton Theological Seminary (~1981–2009).

Donald E. Gjertson specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda, and took up a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst around 1976.

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and Harvard University as a Distinguished Visiting Professor (2004–2010) and Distinguished Visiting Fellow (~2004–2012).
Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Washington University in St. Louis (~1960–1964). He held a post at Emory University from around 1982 to 2022.
Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Ludo Rocher, and Patrick Olivelle.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After doctoral study at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, he held faculty posts at Middlebury College (~1979–1989) and the University of Michigan from 1990.
Dor Bahadur Bista worked in Tibetology. He studied at Tri Chandra College and served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (attested 1988).
Doranne Jacobson works in Indology. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorji Wangchuk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his master's and doctoral degrees at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, joining the Hamburg faculty as professor around 2002.

Dorothy C. Wong specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She has served as a faculty member at the University of Virginia and as a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009).
Douglas Matthew Gildow works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University (attested 2016), supervised by Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.

Douglas Ober specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington (~2008–2010) and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (~2011–2017) under Harjot Oberoi.
